mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-25.9, -21.6, -20.4, -17.3). This momentum reflects a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary shopping and recreation activity that should continue over the next four weeks absent a policy shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite three prior weeks of monotonic improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has been declining each week (14.6, 14.9, 11.7, 10.1), indicating households are spending less time confined at home. If RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 points, this threshold marks a behavioral shift toward normalized out-of-home activity that should push RETAIL_REC higher over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.6 to 10.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a RESIDENTIAL reading below 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rebound in WORKPLACES (from -27.3 to -8.6) and TRANSIT (from -33.1 to -23.7) signals phased lifting of circuit-breaker restrictions. When both series recover together, commuting-linked retail footfall near transit hubs and office districts rises, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise for two consecutive weeks simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility reflects restored mobility infrastructure usage that combines with reduced RESIDENTIAL time to compound retail footfall gains. The interaction of rising TRANSIT/WORKPLACES with falling RESIDENTIAL produces a larger RETAIL_REC increase than any single series alone over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC 4-week mean does not exceed prior 4-week mean despite simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high week-to-week volatility (-20.9, -3.6, -11.1, -16.9) consistent with weather-driven or weekend-concentrated outdoor activity rather than a stable trend. This noisy seasonal signal has no persistent directional relationship with RETAIL_REC and should not predict a sustained shift in retail mobility over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated without a clear trend over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS show a consistent same-direction co-movement over the next week, contradicting the claim of a weak/negative seasonal relationship.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near baseline (-6.3, 0.6, -0.6, -0.6) after an initial stockpiling spike, indicating panic-buying behavior has ended. Once GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within +/-1 point for two consecutive weeks, household spending reallocates toward non-essential retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/-1 point of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has stayed near baseline for the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following two consecutive weeks of stabilized GROCERY_PHARM near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Despite declining, RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 10 points, indicating persistent caution and reduced discretionary outings. In a regime of lingering public fear of infection, even modest RESIDENTIAL declines will not translate into retail recovery, keeping RETAIL_REC growth muted or reversing it over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 points despite decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 points, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved each week for three consecutive weeks (-34.3, -33.1, -28.4, -23.7), reflecting growing willingness to travel. This always-on leading indicator should translate into higher RETAIL_REC in the immediate following week as transit-dependent shoppers resume outings.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following a third consecutive weekly rise in TRANSIT.
